findings.asked: Draw a decay curve, read it, then draw a tangent to find a rate.
findings.wentWrong: The grid scale made a smooth curve hard; readings were generous; only the best drew a tangent for the rate.
findings.rule: Rate of change at a point = gradient of the tangent there.

findings.asked: Draw an exponential graph, read when a value trebled, then find a rate from a tangent.
findings.wentWrong: Most drew the graph (the x = 0 value was the common loss) and read it; only the better candidates drew a tangent and not all found its gradient.
findings.rule: Draw the tangent with a ruler, pick two far-apart points on it, use the scale.

findings.asked: Draw a curve; use it; interpret a gradient.
findings.wentWrong: Curves were good; the usage part was under half; the interpretation of meaning just over half.
findings.rule: Say what the gradient measures in the units of the axes.

ruleToRemember: The gradient at a point on a curve is the gradient of the tangent drawn there; draw it with a ruler, use two distant points and the axis scales, and interpret it with units.
aStarSignal: Drawing a tangent unprompted and turning its gradient into a rate with units.
